content:
To update Members on the
situation around Intake Wood and to formally agree a recovery plan
in light of resident feedback.


a)    
That the recovery plan detailed in the report is
approved and implemented;
 

b)    
That existing funds be utilised to complete these
works as set out; and
 

c)    
That closer links with the local community are
maintained as detailed within the report.

These works will
ultimately help to ensure the Council protects and enhances green
spaces, which is Ambition 6 of our Community Plan, but also ensures
that the authority fulfils its health and safety duties in relation
to the woodland and responds to resident feedback.

Felling work could have
continued as planned, but this would only further have caused
concern within the community.
 
Felling could be paused
until the winter with no restoration works done, but this would
result in the site being left in a state which would leave the
Council liable to possible claims which could occur in the
interim.
topline: The Portfolio Holder - Climate and the Environment has decided to approve a recovery plan for Intake Wood in response to resident feedback.

content:
To secure Portfolio Holder
approval to use Section 106 contributions held by the District
Council for improvements to community sports facilities in
Edwinstowe.
 

That part of the
contribution for community facilities and sports pitch
contributions secured through the s106 Agreement AG1180 and held by
the District Council in the sum of £26,000 to be used as a contribution
towards improvements to the community sports facilities at Thoresby
Sporting Trusts’ ground at Fourth Avenue, Edwinstowe for
improvements to the Clubhouse and the purchase of sporting
equipment for the benefit of all user groups.
 
That the
Council’s Capital Programme is increased by
£26,000 funded
by the community
facilities and sports pitch contribution from
Section 106 agreement AG1180.
 

To support the project
recommended by the Working Group and to enable the s106
contribution for community facilities and sports pitches held for
suitable projects in vicinity of Edwinstowe to be delivered by
Thorsby Sporting Trust in accordance with the terms of agreement
AG1180 to facilitate the delivery of improvements to its
facilities.
 

The Section 106
receipts held under this agreement have
to spent on community facilities and sports pitches in (the
vicinity of the Thoresby Vale site) Edwinstowe within an agreed
timescale in accordance with S106 Agreement AG1180. 
 
This is a project that
can be supported; however, the alternative option is to not support
the project which would then not be delivered. 
 
Accordingly, if
the monies are not spent in accordance with the s106
agreement spend by date the receipt would have to be
repaid to the developer with any interest accrued whilst
the Council has held the contributions. 
Therefore, in
respect of this proposal it is deemed appropriate
to transfer the monies to Thoresby Sporting Trust to use
for the project outlined which will enable the Trust to
improve its facilities and equipment and future proof its continued
offer.
topline: The Leader - Portfolio Holder Strategy, Performance & Finance has decided to allocate £26,000 for improvements to community sports facilities in Edwinstowe.

content:
To seek Portfolio Holder
approval to receive additional £500,000 funding from
Department of Energy, Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) to further the
Councils decarbonisation ambitions. Due to confirmation of
acceptance being required before 20th April 2026, this
requires Portfolio Holder approval to match fund this amount for
2026-27 to enable the co-funding letter to be returned before the
deadline.

That the
Portfolio Holder aqpproves a variation
to the Capital Programme for 2026-27 to increase the budget for
WH:SHF by £1million which includes
a £500,000 grantfrom DESNZ.
 
The
co-funding document will then be signed and returned before the
deadline of 20th April 2026.
 

This
additional funding enables the Council to accelerate our plans to
decarbonise the Councils housing, replace poor performing and
costly heating systems, reducing utility costs for tenants whilst
also contributing to the  decarbonisation agenda.
 
This aligns

a PV Solar Panel scheme to generate efficiency savings and to
reduce carbon emissions at the Club’s Station Road premises
from the s106 contributions secured through agreements AG1308 and
AG1006 and held by the District Council; and
 
That the
Council’s Capital Programme is increased by £47,000
funded by the Community Facilities contribution from Section 106
agreement AG1308 (£41,850.69) and AG1006
(£5,149.31).
 

To enable S106
monies held for suitable projects in Collingham to be
delivered by Collingham Football Club in accordance
with the terms of agreements AG1308 and
AG1006 to facilitate the delivery of a PV Solar
Panel installation to its clubhouse. 

The Section 106
receipts held under these agreements have to spent on community
facilities in the Parish of Collingham and
Brough in accordance with S106 Agreement AG1308 and
AG1006.  
 
Accordingly if the monies are not spent in accordance
with the s106 agreement spend by date the receipt
would have to be repaid to the developer with any
interest accrued whilst the Council has held the
contributions. 
 
Therefore, in
respect of this proposal it is deemed appropriate
to transfer the monies to Collingham Football
Club to use for the project outlined which
will enable the Club to improve its efficiency and
sustainability well into the
future.

content:
The Committee
considered the report of the Business Manager –
Transformation & Service Improvement and the Senior

share with Members the recommendations put forward by the Working
Group and also the Committee’s endorsement where
relevant. 
 
Councillor Rhona
Holloway, Chair of the Working Group, presented the report to
Members which outlined the rationale for the establishment of the
Working Group, which was consideration of activities outside the
Council’s remit and the balance of the benefit to residents
with resource impact.  Topics which the
Working Group considered were detailed within the report with the
proposals detailed in paragraph 2; including flooding – the
effects and prevention; continuity of public health services
delivered by the Council during local government reorganisation;
and planning infrastructure.  An agreed
proposal was to extend an invitation to the Environment Agency (EA)
to attend committee in order to provide
Members with further insight into the EAs role within flood
prevention, as well as key priorities and projects which had been
identified as areas of focus within the County, specifically the
Newark & Sherwood district.  Richard
Cooper of the Environment Agency was in
attendance at the meeting.
 

AGREED    
(unanimously) that the Policy & Performance Improvement
Committee note:

 

a)          
that the Leader of the Council had written to the
Mayor of the East Midlands Combined County Authority on the issue
of Flooding; and
 

b)         
that an invitation had been extended to
representatives of the Environment Agency to discuss and understand
the priorities and areas of focus for this agency within flood
prevention in Newark & Sherwood;
 

AGREED    
(unanimously) that the Policy & Performance Improvement
Committee endorse:

 

c)          
the continuity of public health services provided by
the Council during the Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) and
through the transition process leading up to vesting day,
recommending that the Health Active Lifestyles manager be appointed
to Newark & Sherwood District Council’s LGR
implementation group, once established; and
 

d)         
that an invitation be extended to Planning
Infrastructure colleagues to a future meeting of the Policy &
Performance Improvement Committee, to provide an overview of the
service areas, including cases where operations extend beyond
‘typical’ district council responsibilities.

legal continuity on Right to Buy applications.
content:
This report seeks approval to
request an extension of the Initial Demolition Notices issued as
part of the Yorke Drive Estate Regeneration Project, to ensure
legal continuity on Right to Buy applications.

To support an
application to the Secretary of State to extend the time period for
the initial demolition notices served in relation to the York Drive
Regeneration Scheme.

The justification to
extend the Initial Demolition Notices is grounded in a series of
unprecedented and complex challenges that have impacted project
progression, including the COVID-19 pandemic; the war in Ukraine;
redesign requirements; and the resolution of highways concerns
through the planning process. Extending the notices safeguards the
project’s strategic objectives, and enables the Council to
complete all final acquisitions (including the Compulsory Purchase
Order) whilst preventing the continuation of Right to Buy
applications within the Yorke Drive Regeneration zone.

It continues to be an
option not to extend the Initial Demolition Notices and allow them
to expire. This poses as a high risk to the Council should a tenant
subsequently submit a Right to Buy application due to the
timescales and costs associated with new, fragmented, Compulsory
Purchase Orders. The legal impact of this could be delays of
between 12-18 months on the project programme, leaving the Council
vulnerable to financial penalties and clauses from Lovell due to
the inability to progress the construction programme on
time.
topline: The Portfolio Holder - Housing has decided to request an extension of Initial Demolition Notices for the Yorke Drive Estate Regeneration Project.

topline: The Council has decided to allow the publication of the Nottinghamshire & Nottingham Local Nature Recovery Strategy and provide guidance on its usage in planning and biodiversity assessments.

initiative to green entrances and exits to towns and villages in

topline: The Cabinet has decided to expand a pilot initiative to green entrances and exits to towns and villages in Newark & Sherwood.

content:
To provide an update on recent
grant awards funded through UK Shared Prosperity Fund (UKSPF) and
Rural England Prosperity Fund (REPF).

AGREED that the Portfolio
Holder for Sustainable Economic Development
notes:
 

a)      
The list of successful grant applications recently
awarded grant funding, approved by the Section 151 Officer (in
accordance with the process and criteria approved at Cabinet), to
be funded by UKSPF and REPF, as shown in Appendix A of this
report.
 

The UK Shared Prosperity
Fund and Rural England Prosperity Fund provides funding towards
projects that deliver the Council’s Community Plan objectives
and helps accelerate community, skills and business support
provision across the district. The delivery process undertaken is
objective, open and transparent, avoiding any conflicts of
interest, as set out as a clear requirement within the Governments
Grants Functional Standard, demonstrating a best practice approach
to managing grants.

This report is for the
provision of information and noting. The delivery of the grant
scheme and approval of individual grants follows the process as set
out and approved by Cabinet.
